{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVQjccM8AAAABZabcVQ", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn3IfzhDBvdA", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn3If", "number": 27, "title": "Implement programmable LCD frame timing and registers 0x16–0x17", "body": "## Problem

At baseline `e37a863ad6bf30febeaede058fc052149b1ebe2e`, `bus.rs` rejects every port-0x16 value except 158 and leaves port 0x17 unsupported. CPU word OUT/IN accesses at 0x16 therefore fail on the adjacent high-byte register, even with the accepted default total.

Scanline readback, raster interrupts, timers, rendering and frame completion independently assume 159 lines. The Wasm adapter exposes a constant refresh rate, which the browser caches once. Merely accepting register writes would leave software-visible timing and browser pacing inconsistent.

These failures obstruct legitimate LCD initialization and timing changes across the family. Commercial-title compatibility remains untested.

## Expected outcome

Support LCD total and synchronization programming with coherent scanline/frame progression on WonderSwan, WonderSwan Color and SwanCrystal. For established full-height configurations, port 0x16 specifies the final line: a stable value T produces T+1 lines, each 256 clocks, at the existing 3.072 MHz clock.

Carry actual frame progression through the core, Wasm API and browser pacing. Preserve the 224×144 framebuffer and existing default cadence. Distinguish STN synchronization from Crystal behavior and document unresolved edge policies without claiming physical accuracy.

## Context

Relevant paths are `crates/ws-core/src/{bus.rs,lib.rs,cpu.rs,video.rs}`, `crates/ws-web/src/lib.rs`, `web/src/main.ts`, existing native/browser suites and fixture tooling.

Inspected technical evidence:

- [Wonderful display definitions](https://github.com/WonderfulToolchain/hardware-definitions/blob/46783132a59e576c11456f5997620594eca1c390/target/wswan/display.xml) describe the final-line register, recommend even totals, and identify 0x17 as the WS/WSC STN back-porch control, normally programmed to T−3. This recommendation does not establish that hardware rejects or masks odd values.
- [WSHWTest observations](https://github.com/FluBBaOfWard/WSHWTest/blob/main/README.md) distinguish model startup values, including Crystal synchronization readback. The author qualifies interpretations; these tables are not a complete verified firmware handoff.
- [Pinned ares scheduling](https://github.com/ares-emulator/ares/blob/c76aaffa6e69778baf9a66d1da04298ac2ed7d1d/ares/ws/ppu/ppu.cpp) and [register handling](https://github.com/ares-emulator/ares/blob/c76aaffa6e69778baf9a66d1da04298ac2ed7d1d/ares/ws/ppu/io.cpp) corroborate programmable totals and refresh reporting. They are implementation evidence, not silicon proof; short-frame comments explicitly retain uncertainty. Do not copy emulator code.

Assumption correction: the existing fixed-158 restriction treats a programmable register as an immutable requirement. Replace that restriction using the display definitions above. Preserve 158 as the existing synthetic startup policy unless stronger evidence justifies a separately documented correction.

Main matches the baseline and the open-Issue collection, including PRs, is empty. #25/#26 completed raw cartridge mapping, not LCD timing. [Saved validation](https://github.com/takahirox/wonderswan-rust/blob/e37a863ad6bf30febeaede058fc052149b1ebe2e/docs/issue-25-validation.md) reports 83 core unit tests, ten integration tests and both Chromium suites passing. The gameplay suite initially failed concurrently, then passed alone without changes. These are reported results, not checks rerun during planning.

WSdev Display returned 403; STSWS returned 502; Wonderful rendered display pages were inaccessible. Accessible source alternatives support useful work. Mid-frame latching, very short totals and precise Crystal readback remain research limits.

Scope includes necessary cross-file scheduling and integration work. Full pixel pipelines, analog panel response, unrelated CPU timing and firmware reconstruction remain separate gaps.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] Before scheduler changes, complete a bounded source reconciliation covering total-write activation, shortening below the current line, short/odd totals and Crystal 0x17 behavior. Record inspected references and distinguish established requirements from explicit compatibility policies where evidence remains insufficient. Cover those policies with termination/state-consistency tests; do not present upstream guesses as measured hardware facts. Evidence-based corrections require no human approval or independent AI re-review; record the old assumption, corrected requirement, source and rationale without weakening relevant acceptance.
- [ ] Implement byte accesses to 0x16/0x17 and actual CPU word IN/OUT at 0x16 on all three models. Verify independent register programming and documented readback/model policies. Standard STN programming T−3 must execute successfully. Do not silently force every total back to 158 or automatically rewrite the separately programmed synchronization register.
- [ ] Use coherent raster state for port-2 readback, line wrapping, rendering, line-compare interrupts, HBlank/VBlank timers, VBlank IRQ and existing sprite latching. Exact bus-clock vectors cover stable even totals 156, 158 and 180: respectively 157, 159 and 181 lines, with 40,192, 40,704 and 46,336 clocks per frame. Check boundaries one clock before/after transitions, line 144 events and repeated frames; preserve existing interrupt acknowledgement and timer behavior.
- [ ] Make `frame_number` count actual completed frames monotonically and make `run_frame` follow actual frame completion. Runtime total changes must not reinterpret elapsed clocks, jump the frame count or wait for a stale fixed deadline. Cover increases/decreases, changes during active display/VBlank and instruction/DMA boundary overshoot under the reconciled transition policy. Chunked and single-clock advancement must agree.
- [ ] Keep audio, SDMA, Hyper Voice and EEPROM completion driven by elapsed machine clocks. At nondefault totals, verify audio sample counts from actual clocks and representative DMA event/counter/stall behavior, including a frame crossing. Preserve GDMA/A0 eligibility and costs, model gates and existing SRAM/EEPROM retention; do not rescale device clocks to maintain a fixed samples-per-frame count.
- [ ] Expose current cadence through the thin Wasm adapter and update browser pacing after runtime changes. For stable full-height totals, rate equals 3,072,000 divided by 256(T+1). Preserve bounded catch-up, audio draining, pause/resume, visibility handling, restart/model changes and failed-load recovery. Add deterministic browser scheduling assertions using controlled timestamps and real Wasm execution so a startup-cached frame duration fails the check.
- [ ] Add original, source-included CC0 cartridge coverage that executes byte/word register accesses, programs shorter/longer normal totals and records checked raster/interrupt progress. Run it natively and through the existing production-preview Chromium compatibility flow on all three models, including restart and a runtime timing change. Check execution markers and framebuffer output; require no proprietary ROM, firmware, physical console or human gameplay.
- [ ] Coordinator runs and records `python3 fixtures/build.py --check`, `python3 demo/build.py --check`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo test --workspace --locked`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings`, and `git diff --check`; in `web`, run `npm run build:wasm`, `npm run build`, `npm run test:browser` and `npm run test:compat` against production preview. Run browser suites sequentially given the recorded concurrency failure. Preserve existing three-model gameplay, raw mapping, audio, DMA, saves and console-persistence regressions.
- [ ] Update support documentation, fixture provenance and saved validation with implemented timing, startup/model policies, corrected assumptions and remaining uncertainties. Preserve independent implementation ownership, firmware-free startup, browser-local data and existing architecture. Coordinator completes source-Issue review and resolves blocking findings before merge; distinguish tests present, checks actually passing and optional checks unperformed.

## Optional validation

Additional deterministic software comparisons against independent upstream implementations may inform unresolved transition cases. Such agreement is corroboration, not physical-hardware certification. Report only checks actually performed.

## Required post-merge verification

None

## Specification reconciliation

This task was authored by AI under the agreed WonderSwan-family hardware goal.
Correct erroneous technical assumptions or acceptance criteria when primary hardware
specifications establish the correction. Update this Issue and record the original
assumption, corrected requirement, primary reference and rationale in the PR.
These technical corrections require neither human approval nor an independent AI
re-review. Preserve the agreed goal and relevant pre-merge acceptance; do not weaken
requirements merely to accommodate incomplete implementation or failing tests.
